transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, my daughter thought I should come in. She says I just can't sit still anymore. And, you know, I feel like I’m always up and moving. Even on a quiet day, I’m bouncing from the garden club list to my knitting bag to travel papers before I’ve really finished any one thing. Oh, speaking of travel papers, we're planning a trip to see my sister in Florida. She just got a new dog, a little terrier mix, so cute. I used to have a terrier when I was a girl, feisty little thing named Buster. He used to chase the mailman down the street every single day... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, yes, just always moving around, I guess.
Have you noticed your mood being unusually high or irritable lately, or needing less sleep than usual without feeling tired?

Unusually high? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. Just my normal self. And sleep... well, I sleep my usual amount. I definitely still feel it if I don't get a good night's rest! 

Actually, speaking of sleep, I just bought one of those new memory foam mattress toppers they always advertise on the morning shows. Shirley—she's from my garden club—swore by hers. Said it was like sleeping on a cloud. But honestly, when I opened the plastic, the thing smelled just like a chemical factory. I had to drag it all the way out to the back porch to air it out, and wouldn't you know it, the very next afternoon it started pouring rain! I had to holler for the neighbor boy, Tommy, to help me haul it back inside before it got ruined. He's such a sweet kid, just started classes at the community college for... oh, I think it's business? Or maybe computers, they all do computers now. 

Anyway... wait, what were we talking about? Oh! Moods and sleep. Well, I was a little irritable about the rain on my new mattress pad, but no, nothing unusual overall.
Have you felt down, depressed, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, like your garden club or knitting?

Down? Oh goodness, no. I still absolutely love my knitting and the garden club. In fact, I'm working on a little cardigan right now for my grand-nephew. It's this beautiful soft yellow yarn. I actually found it at that craft shop over on Maple Avenue—you know, the building that used to be the old roller rink back in the seventies? 

Oh, my late husband and I used to go couples skating there all the time. They had this massive disco ball, and they'd play all those wonderful old songs. It's such a shame they paved over the back parking lot to put in that new drive-through pharmacy. Not that the pharmacy isn't convenient, I suppose. I was just there Tuesday to pick up my vitamin C, and the girl at the counter had the most fascinating acrylic nails. They had little tiny rhinestones glued right onto the tips! I just couldn't stop staring at them. I can't imagine how she types on the cash register with those things without popping one off... 

Um... gosh, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh! Being depressed. No, no, I'm happy as a clam. Just always got a lot going on in my head, I suppose.
Do you often find it hard to stay focused on one task, or do you feel like your thoughts are always jumping around from one thing to another?

Well, yes, I suppose my thoughts do jump around quite a bit. Like, I can start out listening at a planning meeting for the garden club, or reading the church bulletin, but after a little while I realize I’ve missed half of what was said or printed. I’ll just be sitting there, and suddenly I’m thinking about the flower arrangements for Sunday service. 

Oh, speaking of Sunday service, Pastor Dave wore the most unusual tie last week. It had these little tiny mallard ducks all over it. I remember my brother used to hunt mallards when we were younger. He had this old hunting dog, a retriever named Duke, who would fetch the ducks right out of the freezing water. Duke was such a good boy, but he smelled terrible when he was wet. Wet dog smell is just the worst, isn't it? I always tell my sister she needs to dry off that new terrier of hers thoroughly if he goes out in the rain, or her whole house will smell like a swamp. 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, staying focused. Yes, I do find it hard sometimes. My mind just goes on a little trip all by itself!
Do you often feel restless or as though you need to keep moving, even when you're trying to relax or be still?

Restless? Well... yes, I suppose I do. If I have to sit still for too long, like watching a movie or sitting in the waiting room, I get this stirred-up feeling inside. It’s like I just need to stand up and straighten something, or go check on something. 

Actually, I was at the dentist's office just last Thursday, waiting for Dr. Miller—he's been my dentist for thirty years, lovely man, though his new hygienist is a bit heavy-handed with the scraper. Anyway, I was sitting in that waiting room, and they have those magazines that are always two years out of date. I found myself flipping through a Better Homes and Gardens from 2021, and there was this article about organizing your pantry with those clear plastic bins. I thought, you know, my pantry is a complete disaster right now. I have three open bags of flour because I can never remember if I have any when I'm at the grocery store. 

Oh! And the grocery store on Elm Street just rearranged their aisles. It is completely maddening. They moved the baking supplies to the very back corner, right next to the pet food. Why would you put flour next to dog kibble? It makes no sense at all. I ran into Mrs. Gable there—she used to teach second grade—and she was just as confused as I was, wandering around looking for powdered sugar...

Gosh, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I'm sorry. You asked if I feel restless. Yes, I do. I just get this urge to get up and do something, anything, rather than just sit there.
